title: Color Theory
summary: Color encodes brand, hierarchy and status; semantic consistency and perception matter more than palette novelty.

MUST.text: Define semantic color tokens for text, surface, action, border and status (success, warning, error, info).
Never communicate status or selection through color alone; add text, icon or shape (see A11Y-002).
Pair colors by lightness difference, not hue alone, so distinctions survive grayscale and color blindness.

SHOULD.text: Test light/dark and increased-contrast themes; remap tokens rather than invert.
Use perceptually uniform spaces (e.g., OKLCH/LCH) when deriving tints and shades.
Limit chromatic accents to meaningful roles; keep neutrals for structure.

AVOID.text: Color-only status indicators or selection states.
Low lightness difference between adjacent semantic colors (e.g., two blues differing only in hue).
Assuming dark mode passes by inverting light-mode values.

DECIDE.decision: Pair with icon/text; ensure grayscale distinction
Reserve for primary actions and key states

EXAMPLE.good: "Error state uses red icon + 'Error' text + red border; passes grayscale."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Status shown only by red vs green dots."

FAILURE_MODES: Color-only cues fail for color-blind users.
Inverted dark-mode palettes drop below contrast thresholds.
Hue-only distinctions collapse in grayscale or print.
Overuse of accent colors dilutes hierarchy.
